column11: derived and found to be nil: AbbVie generated $17,816mm of free cash flow on $61,160mm of revenue in FY2025, a 29.13% margin, against the 28.95% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The two reconcile to within a fifth of a point, which is why this is zero rather than absent: the check was run and it found nothing to charge. Restated before interest: ABBV paid $3,002mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2025, 4.91% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Restated at replacement capex: ABBV spent $1,214mm on plant over 2025 against $762mm of plant depreciation, 0.74% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge stays nil. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 32.46% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2025 supports 38.40%, so the charge rebuilds at -5.94%. It was held at nil, but ABBV books $7,377mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0001551152-26-000008), 12.06% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -5.94%. Restated without working capital build: over 2025 ABBV's cash flow statement shows receivables up $1,490mm, inventories up $234mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $951mm, a working capital build of $773mm, 1.26% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -5.94% to -7.35%.
column12: AbbVie books its amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales, $7,377mm of it, which is why its 29.8% cost of sales is so far above Pfizer's 25.7% and why the same test that charged Pfizer 22% charges AbbVie nothing. The older windows would imply a credit, not a cost: 33.6% over three years and 36.3% over five, both above the model, because they carry peak Humira. A backward window cannot be used to charge a company whose margin is falling

Same disease, same target (IL-13), same self-injected Part D setting. Apogee's Q2 2026 10-Q (0001193125-26-341289) says the Part A doses were designed to equal lebrikizumab's exposures and the Part B high dose to exceed Ebglyss exposures by about 90 to 100%. 2025 is Ebglyss's first full year (approved September 2024). Its beneficiaries averaged 4.45 claims, mostly two-pen induction fills, which is about half of a first-year course. That is the same coverage as the calibrated convention (Dupixent 2025: 6.97 fills of 13), so the launch-year per-claim exception is not taken. The true launch year, 2024 ($17,111 over 168), is not used. Alternatives: Dupixent 2025 $29,950.49 over 165,562 (the comparator the pool's two seeds carry at its 2024 value, but IL-4R and multi-indication); Adbry 2025 $23,459.82 over 3,554 (mature anti-IL-13). Leans high for 2030: FDA approved Ebglyss for one maintenance dose every eight weeks in Q2 2026 (Lilly 8-K 0000059478-26-000077), which cuts its annual cost.

column11: Measured anchor, same class. Adbry, the anti-IL-13 antibody with the longest series, held 2,750 Medicare Part D beneficiaries in 2024, its third full year, against Dupixent's 88,374: 3.112%. Times the 44.27% of moderate-to-severe patients who reach advanced therapy (Haft MA et al., Curr Med Res Opin 2024;40(12):2057-2066, 193 of 436, as the pool's seeds carry it), that is 1.3775% of the pool held in year index 2. Solved on this pool (2,064,000, incidence 64,833, eligible 1.0), this curve (k 0.985, midpoint 1.42) and 25.37% discontinuation, the anchor peak is 0.01226. The capture_anchor identity reproduces it. Year 0: stock 5,170, starts 5,170, pool 2,128,833, rate 0.243%. Year 1: stock 14,542 less 3,859 carried (5,170 x 0.7463) = 10,684 starts over 2,188,496 = 0.488%. Year 2: stock 28,431 less 10,853 carried = 17,578 starts over 2,242,645 = 0.784%, and the stock is 1.38% of the pool. Multiple 1.0, a judgement. For: the best Phase 2 profile in the class (Part B mid dose EASI-75 65.9% vs 23.4% placebo), dosing every three or six months in maintenance, and AbbVie's Rinvoq and Skyrizi field force. Against: it launches in 2030 as the third pipeline claimant here, after amlitelimab (2027) and tilrekimig (2030), into two marketed IL-13s, with Ebglyss now on eight-weekly maintenance. The newest IL-13 is tracking Adbry and not beating it: Ebglyss held 1.84% of Dupixent's beneficiaries in its first full year (3,052 of 165,562) against Adbry's 1.99% in its own (851 of 42,791). The value is half the single-molecule band midpoint amlitelimab carries, which is the low setting a late entrant needs. Crowding: pool_crowding.solve on the three claimants gives no rationed year. It keeps 0.890 of APG777's uncrowded peak, and adding APG777 lowers amlitelimab from 0.952 to 0.915 and tilrekimig from 0.934 to 0.898.
